findings.summary: THE TEST-REVIEWER HALF OF THE REWRITTEN SENTENCE IS NOW EXACT; THE PRODUCTION HALF ATTRIBUTES TO PRODUCTION A RETRACTION THAT IS MINE, AND THAT NO PRODUCTION VERDICT CONTAINS. Verified against .harness/review rather than against the prose. (1) 'THE TEST REVIEWER measured the 2x mutant killed in 3 of 7 runs (~43%: five class-scoped plus two full module runs), bimodal at 3/4, honest never below 6 including at load average 123' is CORRECT and is mine: TR-M4.17-3 (e8a3151c1973, role test-reviewer, task M4.17) reads 'fastRate = 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 over five class-scoped runs -- failures 0, 1, 0, 0, 1 -- plus two full :sequencer:test runs (246 tests) at 1 failure then 0. Killed in 3 of 7 runs, survived in 4. The mutant is bimodal at 3/4 ... Clean honest values: 6 (three idle runs), 6 (two runs under 32 spinners on 20 cores), 7 (two runs at load average 123) ... honest never went below 6 in seven runs, including at load 123.' 3/7 = 42.9%, and it reconciles with M4.41's 'killed 2 of 5 runs' (the class-scoped subset). Nothing in that clause is attributed to me that I did not run. (2) 'which the test reviewer reproduced as `3L to be less than 3L`' is also mine and substantively right: TR-M4.43-1 (961791a88be4, test-reviewer) reports honest slowRate 3 in 4 of 4 runs at the 2000ms window and the resulting red on LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:427's isLessThan(3L). The recorded string is 'Expecting actual: 3L to be less than: 3L' -- the entry drops one colon; not worth a byte of churn, noted only because the clause is inside backticks. (3) THE DEFECT IS 'THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER re-measured independently and RETRACTED its own earlier report that the floor fix held.' Production DID re-measure independently -- three 2000ms runs at fast=6,7,7 in M4.43-R1d (68c714405ad5) -- and production DID once report the floor held (e8a3151c, reviewer, summary point (1): 'the raised rate floor kills multipliedBy(2) -- the mutant lands at exactly 3 against isBetween(4L,30L)'). But no production verdict anywhere retracts it. I listed every verdict for M4.17 and M4.43 in mtime order: e8a3151c is production's LAST M4.17 verdict, and its three later M4.43 verdicts (68c71440, 0d447714, b0a1c839, 57281fcd) never revisit the floor claim. The retraction the sentence describes is MINE, of MY OWN report: TR-M4.17-6 (3893ebde7112, test-reviewer) proposed the floor -- 'the class alone green 5/5 ... the 2x mutant lands EXACTLY on the inclusive floor ... Cheapest remedy: raise the floor from 3 to 4, which kills 2x' -- and TR-M4.17-3 withdrew it: 'THE FLOOR OF 4 DOES NOT KILL multipliedBy(2); it kills it about 40% of the time.' Production said exactly this in the finding being fixed: M4.43-R4a states 'the retraction is TR-M4.17-3, the same role. So the roles are swapped', and its remedy was 'production, three 2000ms runs at 6/7/7 -- or drop the counts'. The fix took the test-reviewer half of that remedy and, for production, kept the retraction clause verbatim minus the words 'single-run'. So M4.43-R4a is HALF fixed, and the surviving half is the same class of error the sentence's own preamble disclaims one clause earlier -- 'ATTRIBUTED PER ROLE AND ONLY AS THE RECORD SUPPORTS IT'.
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is permanent and its entire worth is that its entries are checkable against .harness. A session auditing this escape -- M4.15, M4's VERIFIED.md and milestone review, is the next open row, and review.md's cap rule reads these entries as the evidence for what an escape costs -- greps the harness for a production retraction of the floor claim, finds none, and finds instead a production verdict at the FINAL M4.17 hash still asserting the floor kills the 2x mutant. It then cannot tell whether the entry is wrong or the harness is incomplete, in the one sentence that was rewritten specifically to be checkable. Worse in the same direction as the round-5 finding: it again moves a reviewer's work off the role that did it, this time by crediting production with a self-correction it never made while erasing that the test review corrected ITSELF between two recorded verdicts -- which is the single most useful fact in the whole series, because it is the one that shows the 5/5 'lands EXACTLY on the floor' reading was under-sampled by the same reviewer who later took seven runs. One clause fixes it, and it does not need a new measurement: 'THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER re-measured independently, three runs at the 2000ms window (6/7/7). The retraction was the test review's own: it proposed the floor of 4 from five runs at fastRate=3, then withdrew that from seven.'

findings.summary: DE-NUMBERING THE FINDINGS IS AN HONEST FIX, NOT AN EVASION -- BUT ONE ORDINAL CLAIM SURVIVED IT AND IT IS THE ONE THE RECORD CONTRADICTS. On the honesty question: all four previously narrated findings are still present and still named by what they found (the four-not-two minors with drainPermits lost; M4.42's second duplicate in production; M4.41's doubled remedy numbers and its red on a correct tree; 'the mutant is 7, not 6' plus 'BOTH ROWS'), they map one-to-one onto the four recorded majors, the reason for dropping the numbers is stated rather than silently applied, the opening still concedes 'Past the cap of two', and the authoritative round count is computed from .harness and not from this file. Dropping the numbers also FIXED the substantive half of M4.43-R4b: with the ordinals gone, 'both introduced by the previous round's fixes' is now true (R3a/R3b came from the fix to R2a, the round immediately before), where 'round 2's fixes' was false. What did not survive the record is 'THIS ENTRY CLAIMS NO CONVERGENCE: the final round passed both roles'. The round that passed both roles and returned R3a/R3b is b0a1c839, and by mtime over .harness/review it is the FOURTH of six: 57281fcd (production, changes-requested, carrying the major this delta exists to fix) came after it, and this round comes after that. The entry therefore ends by narrating the process as having converged at the round that passed, two rounds and two further majors before it did -- inside the paragraph headed 'CLAIMS NO CONVERGENCE'. Minor because the do-not-split conclusion holds under any count, the count is recomputed from .harness by anything that cares, and no session is sent to do wrong work.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the permanent record reconciling 'the final round passed both roles' against the harness finds the last recorded verdict for this task before the commit is a changes-requested carrying a major, and has to open .harness to learn which sentence to believe -- the same cost M4.43-R4b priced at minor for the same file. The second-order cost is specific to this entry: its closing sentence is 'this is the SECOND commit this session where choosing to fix minors rather than record them produced the next round's findings', and the reader cannot check that claim against a narrative that stops one round early and omits the two rounds where it was demonstrated. I RECOMMEND NOT FIXING THIS. The entry cannot describe its own final round without invalidating its own hash, and every fix this task has made to this line has been the next round's surface -- which is the entry's own thesis. Record it in the commit body, or make it self-evidently unfalsifiable with 'a later round passed both roles and still returned two new minors'.
